user.title: spdbf Public Transport
user.description: Show public transport stops near a person on the map, using your own DBF (spdbf) server.

data.public_url: Public URL (for links to departure boards)
data.map_stops: Show nearby stops on the map
data.fallback: Use a public DBF instance while yours is unreachable

data_description.server_url: Address of the DBF Docker container on your network, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:8092.
data_description.public_url: Optional. Where you open DBF in a browser, if that differs from the server URL. Each stop links here.
data_description.sources: DB uses DBF's built-in station list (DB InfraGO). Other entries are HAFAS services, e.g. BVG for Berlin buses, trams and U-Bahn.
data_description.departures: Set to 0 to show stops only, without departures.
data_description.merge_duplicates: Show one stop when several nearby stops have exactly the same departures, as BVG lists some stations several times (e.g. Alexanderplatz).
data_description.merge_networks: Show a DB station and the BVG S-/U-Bahn stop of the same station as one stop, e.g. Berlin Savignyplatz and S Savignyplatz. Its departures show all BVG lines plus the DB lines BVG doesn't list, such as regional trains.
data_description.fallback: Off by default. The public instance runs stock DBF: it allows about 10 requests per minute, so only the nearest 3 stops keep updating, and it has no stop search and no coordinates for BVG stops. Your server is retried every minute and used again as soon as it answers.
data_description.fallback_url: Only used when the option above is on.
data_description.map_stops: Off: no stop entities and no polling. The stop search card, departure dialog and trip view still work, and "near you" uses the device's location or this person's.

error.not_dbf: The server answered, but it doesn't look like DBF.

abort.already_configured: Nearby stops are already set up for this person or device.

missing_coordinates.title: spdbf doesn't send coordinates for some stops
missing_coordinates.description:
The DBF server at {server} returns HAFAS stops (such as BVG) without latitude and longitude, so they can't be shown on the map. DB stops still work.

To fix this, run the patched DBF image `ghcr.io/drakknar/db-fakedisplay` (see github.com/Drakknar/db-fakedisplay-patched). This notice disappears by itself once the server sends coordinates.
